q: What law that describes the force of attraction or repulsion between two charges is directly proportional to their strengths and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them?
a: Coulomb’s law or law of electrostatics

q: What is the rated lifetime of an LED?
exp: LEDs have an extremely long operational life (up to 200,000 hours), compared to approximately 1,000 hours for incandescent bulbs.

q: What coaxial cable type is used for Thick Ethernet?
exp: Thick Ethernet (10Base5) uses RG-11 or RG-8 50-ohm coaxial cable with vampire taps; RG-58 is used for Thin Ethernet (10Base2).

q: What is the typical gain for a rhombic antenna?
exp: Rhombic antennas are large wire antennas used for HF communication. Their gain ranges from 15-60 dB depending on the number of wavelengths per side, making them excellent for long-distance HF work.

q: What is Norton's theorem?
a: Any linear circuit can be replaced by a current source (In) in parallel with a resistance (Rn)
exp: Norton's theorem is the current-source dual of Thevenin's; the Norton current equals the short-circuit current, and Rn = Rth.

q: What characterizes synchronous data transmission?
a: Uses unique SYN characters at the start of each message block
exp: Synchronous transmission sends blocks of data framed by SYN characters, with continuous clocking and no gaps between characters.

q: What is the bandwidth of Ultra Wideband (UWB)?
exp: UWB is defined as having a bandwidth of at least 500 MHz or a fractional bandwidth greater than 20%, enabling high-resolution ranging and high data rates.

q: What is the main advantage of DSBSC over DSBFC?
a: No transmitter power is wasted in the carrier
exp: In double-sideband suppressed carrier (DSBSC), no power is sent in the unmodulated carrier, making it more power-efficient than DSB full carrier.

q: What family of standards defines RS-232C interchange circuits?
exp: V.24 defines the interchange circuits for DTE-DCE interfaces, essentially standardizing what RS-232C calls its 25-pin interface signals.

q: What is the speed of sound at 25°C in sea water?
exp: Sea water at 25°C transmits sound at ~1520 m/s. Sonar and submarine communications rely on this acoustic property.

q: What is the speed of sound in steel at 1 atm?
exp: Sound travels much faster through solids than air. Steel: ~5150 m/s, Wood: ~3300 m/s, Air at 20°C: ~343 m/s, Sea water: ~1520 m/s.

q: What became CDMA 2000?
exp: IS-95 (cdmaOne) evolved into CDMA2000 (IS-2000), a 3G standard. CDMA2000 1xRTT provides 144 kbps and EV-DO provides up to 2.4 Mbps.

q: When was the first cellular commercial system introduced?
exp: Ameritech launched the first commercial cellular telephone network in the US in Chicago, Illinois on October 13, 1983, using the AMPS standard.

q: What is the human hearing range in octaves?
exp: The human ear can perceive sounds from approximately 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz, which spans 10 octaves (each octave doubles the frequency).

What is the number of HDTV horizontal lines?

What is a modem's primary function?
a: Interfaces DTE to an analogue transmission line by modulating/demodulating signals
exp: A modem (modulator-demodulator) converts digital DTE signals to analog for transmission over telephone lines, and reverses the process on reception.

q: What is VRC in data communications?
a: Vertical Redundancy Check — a single parity bit per character
exp: VRC (also called parity check) adds one bit to each character to make the total number of 1s either odd or even, detecting single-bit errors.

q: What is Nikola Tesla known for in electrical engineering?
a: Invention of the AC induction motor and AC power system; the Tesla (unit of magnetic flux density) honors him
exp: Tesla's AC polyphase system became the standard for power distribution. He also developed the Tesla coil, radio (contested), and numerous other electrical inventions.

q: In CATV, what is the noise figure for mid, high, and super band channels?
exp: CATV system noise figures: Sub and low bands ≤5 dB, Mid/High/Super bands ≤6 dB, UHF channels ≤9 dB. Lower noise figures mean better signal quality.

q: What do you call an amplifier that is biased to class C but modulates over the same portion of the curve as if it were biased to class B?
What network topology provides the highest redundancy with no bottlenecks?
exp: In a full mesh topology, every node connects directly to every other node, providing multiple redundant paths and eliminating single points of failure.

What is the difference between a JFET and a MOSFET?
The ability of a material to resist current flow is called “resistance”. What is (are) the factor(s) that affect its value?
What compression law is used in North American telephone systems?
exp: North America and Japan use µ-law (with µ=255) companding for PCM telephony. Europe uses A-law (A=87.6). Both give 8-bit PCM 64 kbps quality.

q: What is differential PCM (DPCM)?
a: PCM that encodes and transmits only the difference between successive samples instead of full sample values
exp: DPCM exploits sample-to-sample correlation in speech to reduce bit rate. The decoder accumulates differences to reconstruct the original signal.

q: How does permittivity affect electric field intensity?
a: It causes the field intensity to decrease.

q: Why is a geostationary satellite not stationary for regions near the poles?
a: The angle of inclination is too low for these regions
exp: Geostationary satellites orbit above the equator (0° inclination). Near the poles, they appear very low on the horizon (<5°), causing blockage and poor signal geometry.

What is the purpose of a squelch circuit?
a: Prevents amplified noise from reaching the loudspeaker when no signal is present
exp: Squelch mutes the audio output when the received signal drops below a threshold, eliminating the noise heard between transmissions.

q: What factors determine the capacitance of a capacitor?
a: Area of the plates, distance between the plates, and the dielectric constant of the material between the plates

q: A full 360° sine-wave signal is applied as an input to an unknown class of amplifier, if the output delivers only a pulse of less than 180°, of what class does this amplifier belongs?
What is the method of reducing reverberation using loudspeaker feedback?
exp: Ambiophony uses electronic feedback to artificially extend or reduce reverberation, creating ideal acoustic conditions in a room.

q: A 50Ω resistor is connected in series with a 150C resistor and to a supply voltage of 20V. What is the current through the 50Ω resistor?
What data compression technique assigns shorter codes to the most frequent characters?
exp: Huffman coding builds a variable-length code tree based on symbol frequency, giving shorter codes to more common characters for data compression.

q: When was the electric telegraph invented?
exp: Samuel Morse demonstrated the electric telegraph on May 24, 1844, sending 'What hath God wrought' from Washington D.C. to Baltimore.

q: What is the principle musical interval considered dissonant?
exp: The ratio 7:8 represents a minor second interval, which sounds tense and dissonant. Consonant intervals include octave (1:2), perfect fifth (2:3), etc.

q: Which of the following is designated as the international distress, safety and calling frequency for radio telephony for stations of the maritime mobile service when using frequencies in the authorized bands between 156 MHz and 174 MHz?
What LAN software prevents simultaneous access to data being modified?
exp: Record locking prevents data corruption in client-server LANs. When one station modifies a record, it's locked so others can read but not simultaneously modify it.

q: What is any tone produced by a sound source in addition to the fundamental tone?
exp: Overtones (harmonics) are integer multiples of the fundamental frequency. They give each instrument its unique timbre.

q: If atomic masses of Al and O are 26.98 amu and 16.00 amu, respectively, how many grams of Al are there in 431g of Al2O3?
What is the science that describes and predicts the effect on bodies at rest or in motion by forces acting on it?
What is the IMT-2000 maximum data rate for mobile users in high-speed vehicles?
exp: IMT-2000 (3G) specifications: 144 kbps for fast-moving vehicles, 384 kbps for pedestrians, and over 2 Mbps for stationary/indoor users.

q: When a mobile is simultaneously in the coverage area of two base stations, this is called?
exp: Soft handoff (CDMA) maintains connections to both base stations simultaneously before dropping one. TDMA/GSM uses hard handoff (break-before-make).

q: What is defined as the ratio of the change in temperature to the change in pressure when a real gas is throttled?
What is the frequency one octave above middle C?
exp: One octave above middle C (262 Hz) is 524 Hz — exactly double. Each octave doubles the frequency.

q: What do you call a positively charged ion?
What is the height of GLONASS satellites?
exp: GLONASS satellites orbit at approximately 19,100 km altitude in 64.8° inclined orbits, slightly lower than GPS at ~20,200 km.

What is the Kell factor (utilization factor) for TV vertical resolution?
exp: The Kell factor reduces effective vertical resolution to about 70% of the total line count, due to the sampling nature of the scanning process.

q: What is the main disadvantage of fiber optic cable made of glass?
exp: Glass fiber is fragile and can break under mechanical stress. It requires careful handling, proper strain relief, and protective jacketing to prevent breaks.

q: What camera tube uses lead oxide and has minimum lag?
exp: The Plumbicon uses lead oxide (PbO) as its photoconductor. Its near-zero lag makes it ideal for live TV — fast motion produces no image retention/smearing.

q: What is the midrange frequency region of the musical sound spectrum?
exp: The midrange covers the most critical musical frequencies where human hearing is most sensitive and instruments' fundamental tones are prominent.

How high above the fielder's glove does the ball pass?
exp: Schaum's College Physics - Uniformly Accelerated Motion

What is Time Division Multiplexing (TDM)?
a: Each information signal is allowed to use all the available bandwidth but only for a fraction of the time
exp: TDM interleaves time slots from multiple channels into one transmission stream. Used in T1/E1 systems, SONET/SDH, and digital cellular.

q: A 0.50-kg ball falls past a window that is 1.50 m in vertical length. (a) How much did the KE of the ball increase as it fell past the window? (b) If its speed was 3.0 m/s at the top of the window, what was its speed at the bottom?
exp: Schaum's College Physics - Projectile Motion

exp: In CSMA/CD Ethernet, contention (collision) occurs when two stations transmit simultaneously. Both stop, wait a random backoff time, then retry. The listening period is 9.6 µs.

q: What is the typical loudness level of a watch ticking?
exp: A ticking watch produces a very faint sound, measured at approximately 20 phons — just above the threshold of normal hearing.

q: What is the oldest type of semiconductor device used in microwave frequencies?
exp: The point contact diode was the first semiconductor microwave device, used in crystal radio receivers and early radar systems.

q: What is residual magnetism?
a: The flux density, which exist in the iron core when the magnetic field intensity is reduced to zero.

q: What is the envelope delay distortion reference frequency for SSB?
exp: Envelope delay distortion (EDD) is worst at band edges. For SSB voice channels, 1800 Hz is used as the reference frequency for EDD measurements because it's near the center of the 300-3400 Hz voice band.

exp: Schaum's College Physics - Projectile Motion

q: What is the Ethernet preamble for?
a: Synchronizing the receiver clock before data arrives
exp: Ethernet frames begin with 7 bytes of 10101010... followed by SFD byte 10101011. This allows the receiver PLL to synchronize before actual frame data arrives, preventing loss of the first data bytes.

q: What is RZ (Return-to-Zero) signaling?
a: A line code where the signal returns to zero at the end of each bit period
exp: RZ codes return to zero mid-bit, providing clock information embedded in the signal but requiring twice the bandwidth of NRZ for the same bit rate.

a: Array of dipoles with equal spacing, same phase, connected to same source — maximum radiation perpendicular to array axis

What is the upstream signal frequency range in a two-wire CATV cable?
exp: CATV systems use a split-band design: upstream (subscriber-to-headend) uses 5–30 MHz, downstream uses 54–750+ MHz.

q: What is the interval between going off-hook and hearing a dial tone?
exp: Dial tone delay is the time from when a subscriber lifts the handset (goes off-hook) until the CO sends dial tone. It should be less than 3 seconds per ITU standards.

exp: The helical slow-wave structure reduces the phase velocity of the RF wave to match the electron beam velocity (~10-20% of light speed), enabling continuous energy transfer from electrons to the RF wave.

q: What is flat-topped sampling?
a: Sampling using a sample-and-hold circuit, giving each pulse constant amplitude for its full duration
exp: Flat-topped sampling creates rectangular pulses whose amplitude equals the signal at the sampling instant, simplifying digital encoding.

q: What is the guardband for C-band satellite communications?
exp: C-band satellite transponders are typically 36 MHz wide with 4 MHz guardbands between them, allowing 500 MHz of spectrum to accommodate 12 transponders.

q: When was the telephone invented?
exp: Alexander Graham Bell received the patent for the telephone on March 7, 1876, making the first successful voice transmission the next day.

What did John Ambrose Fleming invent?
exp: Fleming invented the thermionic diode valve, the first practical vacuum tube and the foundation of electronic amplification and radio detection.

q: What is the standard pitch frequency for American Concert A?
exp: A4 (Concert A) is universally tuned to 440 Hz. This is the reference pitch used for tuning instruments.

q: What is the exact frequency of the color subcarrier signal?
exp: The NTSC color subcarrier is precisely 3.579545 MHz. This specific frequency was chosen to minimize visible interference between the chroma signal and other TV signals.

q: How do you classify an amplifier used to amplify either amplitude modulated (AM) or frequency modulated (FM) signals?
What is the approximate height of a GEO satellite (from Kepler's law)?
exp: Using Kepler's third law with a 24-hour period, the GEO orbit radius is 42,164 km from Earth's center, giving an altitude of ~35,786 km above the surface.

q: How much more information does HDTV contain compared to NTSC?
exp: HDTV has about 5 times the picture information of NTSC, due to higher resolution (1080 or 720 lines vs 480) and widescreen format.

q: Determine which statement is true?
a: The current carriers in conductors are valence electrons.

q: Which pulse in V blanking corresponds to 3H lines wide?
exp: The vertical sync pulse occupies exactly 3 horizontal line periods (3H). This wide pulse distinguishes it from equalizing pulses (H/2) during vertical blanking.

q: At what temperature should a crystal microphone not be used?
exp: Crystal microphones use piezoelectric crystals that can be damaged or depolarized by heat above approximately 52°C (125°F).

q: What is the SCA subcarrier frequency in FM broadcasting?
exp: The 67 kHz SCA (Subsidiary Communications Authorization) subcarrier carries auxiliary services like store music or reading services for the visually impaired.

q: What OSI layer handles interhost communications?
exp: The Session layer establishes, manages, and terminates sessions between applications on different hosts, including synchronization and dialog control.

q: What is the cut-off frequency of the standard FM pre-emphasis/de-emphasis network?
exp: The 75 µs time constant used in North American FM corresponds to a cut-off frequency of 1/(2π×75×10⁻⁶) ≈ 2122 Hz.

q: What digital modulation does SPADE (satellite) use?
exp: SPADE (Single channel Per carrier, Demand-Assigned, multiple-access Equipment) uses QPSK modulation for efficient use of satellite bandwidth.

q: What refers to a series of tones that sounds good when used in combination?
exp: A musical scale is a set of pitches in ascending or descending order. The diatonic scale is full of consonant tones.

exp: UHF TV channel 28 occupies 554–560 MHz. The picture carrier is at 555.25 MHz; the aural (sound) carrier is 4.5 MHz higher at 559.75 MHz.

How is dynamic convergence adjusted in a color CRT?
a: By varying the current through convergence coils (electromagnets)
exp: Dynamic convergence corrects beam convergence across the entire screen using coils fed with correction waveforms synchronized to the scan.

q: What is a quadrature detector used for in TV?
a: FM detection (demodulation of the audio carrier in TV receivers)
exp: The quadrature detector is widely used for demodulating the 4.5 MHz FM audio carrier in TV receivers; it compares the signal with a 90° phase-shifted version.

exp: AMPS cellular uses FM with ±12 kHz maximum deviation on 30 kHz channel spacing. The 10 kHz supervisory tone is used for handoff signaling.

q: What is the amount of sound attenuation offered by a wall, ceiling, or floor?
exp: Transmission Loss (TL) measures how much a barrier reduces sound. Heavy, dense materials provide greater transmission loss.

q: What is the term for ordinary telephone?
exp: POTS refers to the traditional analog telephone system using the public switched telephone network (PSTN). It has been largely replaced by VoIP and digital systems, but the term is still used.

q: What is the front porch in a TV composite video signal?
a: The brief blanking interval between the end of active video and the horizontal sync pulse
exp: The front porch is a short black level period before the sync pulse, ensuring the sync tip is clearly distinguishable from the video content.

q: What is lowers the operating temperature of receivers to reduce noise levels?
exp: Cryogenic cooling (liquid helium, ~4K) reduces thermal noise in amplifiers to near zero, giving noise figures below 0.1 dB. Used in radio telescopes and satellite ground stations for maximum sensitivity.

q: What is the 10BaseT Ethernet system restricted to?
exp: 10BaseT (twisted pair Ethernet) has a maximum segment length of 100 meters between station and hub/switch. This is due to signal attenuation and CSMA/CD timing requirements.

q: What is the spacing between M88 loading coils on telephone cables?
exp: M88 loading coils (88 mH inductance) are placed at 9000 ft intervals on telephone cables to improve voice frequency transmission by reducing attenuation.

q: What is aliasing (foldover distortion)?
a: Distortion caused by sampling at a rate lower than twice the highest signal frequency
exp: Aliasing occurs when sampling rate < 2 × fmax; the undersampled high frequencies 'fold over' and appear as low-frequency distortion in the recovered signal.

q: What is MPEG-2 primarily used for?
a: Digital broadcast TV (DVD, satellite TV, cable TV) using cosine transform compression
exp: MPEG-2 (ISO 13818) uses the discrete cosine transform for video compression, achieving HDTV quality at 15-20 Mbps. It is the standard for DVD and most broadcast digital TV.

q: Which coaxial connector is more complex but better maintains electrical characteristics?
exp: Type N connectors (named after Paul Neill) are precision RF connectors rated to 18 GHz. They maintain 50 Ω impedance through the connection, unlike cheaper BNC connectors.

q: What accessory is referred to as a magic T?
exp: A Hybrid T (Magic T) is a waveguide junction that splits power equally between two ports while isolating them from each other. It's used in balanced mixers and duplexers.

a: A travelling wave antenna in the shape of a rhombus (diamond), used for HF communications

q: What packets switched data technique is used with GSM systems?
exp: GPRS adds packet-switching capability to GSM's circuit-switched voice network. Data is sent in packets over unused voice time slots, enabling efficient data transmission.

In semiconductor application, which of the following statement is not true?
a: An ohmmeter test across the base-collector of a transistor should show low resistance for both polarities.

q: What do you call the phenomenon whereby substance attracts pieces of iron?
What is the approximate critical frequency of the F2 layer?
exp: The F2 layer (highest ionospheric layer) has a critical frequency of about 8 MHz. Signals below this frequency are reflected back; above it, they pass through. The MUF is about 3× the critical frequency.

q: What is the USSR-developed high-power microwave oscillator?
exp: A gyrotron uses cyclotron resonance to generate millimeter-wave radiation at very high power (megawatts). Developed in the USSR, it's used for plasma heating in fusion research reactors.

q: What frequency band do satellites use with 14–17 GHz uplink and 17–20 GHz downlink?
exp: Ka band (26.5–40 GHz) satellites use approximately 28–30 GHz uplink and 18–20 GHz downlink. Higher frequencies allow smaller antennas and higher data rates.

q: In 1784, who demonstrated that the force between charges is inversely related to the square of the distance between them?
What is the maximum VF tone level that may be fed into a voice signal?
exp: The maximum volume of tone placed on a voice channel is +6 dBm (VU). Exceeding this causes clipping and distortion. Normal speech averages around -15 to -10 dBm on the telephone network.

q: What is the law whereby the force of attraction or repulsion between poles is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them?
What is the prime time block for FM radio in Metro Manila?
What refers to the listing of the date and time events, programs, equipment, test, malfunctions and corrections in communication system?
How many number of atoms are there in 1.32 x 10^3 g of Lead (Pb)? Pb atomic mass is 207.7g.
What is the dielectric constant of polyethylene insulator?
exp: Polyethylene has a relative permittivity (dielectric constant) of 2.27, giving it a velocity factor of about 1/√2.27 ≈ 0.664 in coaxial cable, affecting signal propagation speed.

q: What is an Ionosonde used for?
a: Measures virtual height of the ionosphere
exp: An ionosonde transmits swept-frequency radio pulses upward and measures the return time. The frequency at which pulses stop returning gives the critical frequency; return time gives the virtual height of each ionospheric layer.

q: What is the location of a celestial body in space called?
exp: Ephemeris data describes a satellite's precise orbital parameters at a given time. GPS receivers download current ephemeris data from satellites to calculate exact satellite positions for accurate ranging.

q: What is the inclination of GLONASS satellite orbits?
exp: GLONASS satellites orbit at 64.8° inclination compared to GPS at 55°, giving GLONASS better coverage at high latitudes (like Russia).

q: What is a diplexer used for in a TV antenna system?
a: Prevents FM broadcast signals from entering the TV receiver
exp: A diplexer separates UHF and VHF TV signals while also blocking FM signals (88-108 MHz) from interfering with VHF TV channels.

q: What is AFC in radio receivers?
a: Automatic Frequency Control — feedback system to correct frequency drift in VHF/UHF/microwave receivers
exp: AFC uses a frequency discriminator output to generate a control voltage that keeps the local oscillator on frequency, preventing drift.

q: What form of energy refers to those a system possesses as a whole with respect to some outside reference frame, such as potential and kinetic energies?
What is the first note of the musical scale called?
exp: The root note (tonic) is the starting pitch of a scale. For example, C is the root of the C major scale.

q: What is a balun used for?
a: To connect coaxial cable (unbalanced) to a balanced parallel wire transmission line
exp: A balun (balanced-unbalanced transformer) matches coaxial feed lines to balanced antennas like dipoles, preventing pattern distortion.

q: What is the cause of a minimum Q on a single-tuned LC circuit?

A gun is shot into a 0.50 kN block which is hanging from a rope of 1.8 m long. The weight of the bullet is equal to 5 N with a muzzle velocity of 320 m/s. How high will the block swing after it was hit by the bullet?
What is a 100 Mbps LAN signaling standard using fiber optics?
exp: FDDI uses token-ring topology over dual fiber rings at 100 Mbps. It also runs on coaxial cable. Designed for campus backbone networks before Gigabit Ethernet displaced it.

q: What is blank and burst in AMPS cellular?
a: Interrupting voice to send digital control signals
exp: AMPS blank-and-burst briefly mutes the voice channel to transmit digital control messages such as handoff orders and power control commands. The interruption lasts only milliseconds - completely inaudible to the user.

q: What is Ohm's Law named after?
a: Georg Simon Ohm, who described the relationship V = IR
exp: Ohm's Law (V = IR) states that voltage equals current times resistance, the fundamental relationship in circuit analysis.

q: What refers to a slender member which prevents parts of a structure moving towards each other under compressive force?

What statement of the second law of thermodynamics states that it is impossible to build a device that operates in a cycle and produces no effect other than the transfer of heat from a lower-temperature body to a higher-temperature body?
What is the area above a vertical antenna with no radiation?
exp: Vertical antennas have a null directly overhead (90° elevation). Aircraft flying overhead may lose contact — this dead zone is the curve of silence.

q: What refers to the amount of heat removed from the cooled space in BTS’s for 1 watt-hour of electricity consumed?
What is a plug-in circuit board containing hardware and firmware to connect a computer to a LAN?
exp: The NIC (network adapter) handles all physical layer functions: framing, encoding, CSMA/CD, and media access. It contains both BNC (coax) and RJ-45 (twisted pair) connectors.

q: How will you minimize the output offset voltage due to the input offset current of an op- amp?
What is perigee in satellite orbit?
a: The point in a satellite's orbit closest to Earth
exp: Perigee is the orbit's closest point to Earth; apogee is the farthest. Satellite speed is greatest at perigee.

q: Absolutely, when can we say that the circuit is at resonance?
a: when the voltage and current are in-phase

q: What is the amount of heat needed to turn 1kg of the substance at its boiling point from the liquid to the gaseous state?

The acceleration due to gravity on the moon is 1.67m/s2. If an astronaut can throw a ball 10 m straight upward on earth, how high should this man be able to throw the ball on the moon? Assume that the throwing speeds are the same in the two cases.
What allows one antenna to be used for reception and transmission without mutual interference?
exp: A duplexer connects both transmitter and receiver to a single antenna. It uses filters to isolate Tx from Rx, preventing Tx power from damaging the Rx front end.

q: What logical state is the start bit in asynchronous serial transmission?
exp: In async serial, the line idles at logic 1 (mark). A start bit is always logic 0, signaling the beginning of a character transmission.

q: In statistics, the standard deviation means?

exp: Schaum's College Physics - Uniformly Accelerated Motion

q: What utilizes electrical energy in electrical circuits?
What is Celotex used for in acoustics?
exp: Celotex fiberboard (made from sugarcane bagasse) provides good broadband sound absorption due to its porous fiber structure. Used in recording studios and acoustic treatment as an environmentally friendly, cost-effective absorber.

q: A magnifying glass has a lens with an index of refraction 5.4 and radii of curvature of 2.95 feet and 4.27 feet for the two faces. What is the magnification of the lens when it is held 2.36 inches from an object being viewed?
What is the sonic time pattern called?
exp: Rhythm refers to the pattern of sounds and silences in music — the temporal organization of beats and accents.

q: What is Cheapernet?
a: Another name for Thin Ethernet (10Base2, uses RG-58 coax)
exp: Cheapernet or Thin Ethernet uses 50-ohm RG-58 coaxial cable with BNC connectors, cheaper and less rigid than thick Ethernet (Thicknet).

q: What law created the national council for the promotion of E-Commerce in the country?
What is an optoacoustic transducer?
a: A device that converts light energy into sound
exp: Optoacoustic (photoacoustic) transducers use light absorption to generate acoustic waves, used in medical imaging and gas sensing.

q: What is the wavelength of 30 MHz radio waves?
exp: λ = c/f = 3×10⁸/30×10⁶ = 10 meters. 30 MHz is in the HF band (high frequency), useful for long-distance ionospheric propagation.

q: What is Alternate Mark Inversion (AMI)?
a: A bipolar line code where 1s alternate between positive and negative polarity, and 0s are zero volts
exp: AMI eliminates DC components and provides error detection (a violation occurs if two consecutive marks have the same polarity). Used in T1 transmission.

q: What is companding?
a: Combination of compression at the transmitter and expansion at the receiver to improve SNR for low-level signals
exp: Companding (compress + expand) protects small signals from quantizing noise by applying more gain to weak signals before encoding and less after decoding.

q: What is the resonant frequency of a circuit when L of 3 microhenry and C of 40 picofarad are in series?
What do you call materials, which possess very high permeabilities?
What is lossless data compression?
a: Compression that reduces bit rate without any loss of data quality, using redundancy elimination
exp: Lossless compression (ZIP, PNG, Huffman coding) perfectly reconstructs original data. Compression ratios are typically 2:1 to 5:1.

q: In semiconductor materials, electrons have a higher value of mobility than holes, but which semiconductor material has the slowest electron-mobility?
Why do most long-distance fiber systems use 1550 nm wavelength?
a: Because the loss in glass fiber is lowest at approximately 1550 nm
exp: Silica glass fiber has minimum attenuation (~0.2 dB/km) at 1550 nm. Erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFA) also operate in this window, making it ideal for long-haul transmission.

q: What will happen to a parallel ac-circuit if its line frequency is more than the resonant frequency?

What is the maximum data rate achievable in a fiber optic system?
a: Up to 10 Gbps (per wavelength; much higher with WDM)
exp: Single-channel fiber supports 10 Gbps+; with wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM), aggregate rates of terabits per second are achievable.

q: A 50 watt incandescent lamp has a mean spherical luminous intensity of 66.5 candelas. Compute the total luminous flux radiated by the lamp?
What does MP3 stand for?
a: MPEG-1 Audio Layer 3 (Motion Picture Experts Group 1, Audio Layer 3)
exp: MP3 is a lossy audio compression format that reduces file size by ~90% by removing sounds the human ear is less sensitive to, based on psychoacoustic models.

q: What is the NTSC TV vertical field rate?
exp: NTSC uses 60 fields/second (two interlaced fields make one 30 fps frame). This 60 Hz was chosen to match the North American power line frequency.

q: What type of absorption loss in optical fiber is caused by valence electrons in silica?
exp: UV absorption occurs when photons excite electrons in silica, causing signal attenuation at shorter wavelengths.

q: Why can LORAN C not provide bearing information?
a: LORAN C is a hyperbolic system giving position only, not a directional bearing system
exp: LORAN-C provides location by measuring time differences of signals from multiple stations; it cannot provide bearing like VOR or TACAN.

A ball was dropped into a hard court from a height of 10 m. If the coefficient of restitution is 0.95, what height it will attain on its 5th bounce?
What is the maximum diameter formula for a fiber optic cable?
exp: The maximum core radius for single-mode operation is given by rmax = 0.383λ/NA, ensuring only one propagation mode is supported.

q: What law created the Videogram Regulatory Board (VRB)?
What antenna property is proportional to antenna gain?
exp: The effective aperture or capture area of an antenna is directly proportional to its gain, meaning high-gain antennas intercept more signal.

q: How many holes does the shadow mask of a color CRT have?
exp: The shadow mask is a thin metal plate with ~300,000 tiny holes positioned so each electron beam can only hit its correct color phosphor dot.

q: Which material has the least number of valence electrons?
What is the speech coding rate of D-AMPS?
exp: D-AMPS (IS-136) uses VSELP (Vector-Sum Excited Linear Prediction) codec at 8 kbps. This is half of GSM's 13 kbps, fitting 3 calls into one 30 kHz AMPS channel.

q: A light bulb is used to light a bunker 10 ft below. A chair sits on the floor of the bunker 3 feet from a spot directly below the bulb. What is the illumination on the floor around the chair if the luminous intensity is 150 candles?
What is VDSL speed?
exp: VDSL achieves 52 Mbps downstream over copper loops shorter than 300 meters. Used in FTTN (fiber-to-the-node) deployments. VDSL2 reaches 100+ Mbps symmetrically. Asymmetry reflects typical internet usage patterns.

q: What will happen to the power handling capability of the diode if it is to be operated at a higher temperature?
What is the typical output power of a standard klystron?
exp: High-power klystrons used in particle accelerators and radar systems can produce 10 MW or more of pulsed microwave power. Continuous wave (CW) klystrons for satellite uplinks produce kilowatts.

q: What is the extremely large amount of energy associated with the strong bonds within the nucleus of the atom itself called?
What is the NE602 IC used for?
a: A differential amplifier with on-chip oscillator, used as an RF mixer/oscillator
exp: The NE602 (SA602) is a double-balanced mixer with an internal oscillator, popular for frequency conversion in radio receivers.

q: What is CDMA2000?
exp: CDMA2000 evolved from IS-95 cdmaOne. 1xRTT provides 153 kbps. EV-DO Rev A provides 3.1 Mbps download. Used by Verizon and Sprint in the US before migration to 4G LTE. Same 1.25 MHz channel as IS-95.

q: Why is the resistance of a conductor different for RF current than for DC?
A tennis ball is dropped into a cement floor from a height of 2 m. It rebounds to a height of 1.8 m. What fraction of energy did it lose in the process of striking the floor?

A hose lying on the ground shoots a stream of water upward at an angle of 408 to the horizontal. The speed of the water is 20 m/s as it leaves the hose. How high up will it strike a wall which is 8.0 m away?
exp: Schaum's College Physics - Uniformly Accelerated Motion

q: What is Tinnitus caused by?
a: Exposure to high levels of noise
exp: Tinnitus (ringing ears) results from noise-induced damage to cochlear hair cells above 85 dB SPL. Damaged cells fire spontaneously, creating perceived sound. Affects over 750 million people globally and is generally irreversible.

q: What is the disadvantage of plastic fiber over glass fiber?
exp: Plastic optical fiber (POF) has attenuation of 100–1000 dB/km versus 0.2–3 dB/km for glass, limiting it to very short distances (up to about 100 m).

q: What is the function of a hybrid in a telephone handset?
a: Decrease mic signal in phones (2-wire to 4-wire conversion)
exp: The hybrid transformer converts between 2-wire (local loop) and 4-wire (separate Tx/Rx). It provides sidetone reduction so your own voice doesn't sound too loud in the earpiece.

q: What is quantizing noise?
a: Inaccuracies in PCM caused by representing a continuous signal as one of a finite number of discrete levels
exp: Quantizing error is the difference between the actual sample value and the nearest quantization level. More bits per sample reduces this noise.

q: What is the Hall Effect?
a: When current flows in a conductor in a magnetic field, a voltage appears perpendicular to both
exp: The Hall effect, discovered by Edwin Hall in 1879, produces a transverse voltage when current-carrying conductors are in a magnetic field, used in sensors and measurement.

q: How many voiceband channels are in a master group per CCITT?
exp: Per CCITT, a master group contains 300 voiceband channels, formed by combining multiple supergroups.

q: When comparing rms voltages and average voltages, which of the following statement is true, assuming sine waves?
a: The rms voltage is always greater than the average voltage

q: How does cavity resonator Q factor relate to frequency?
a: Q increases with frequency (smaller dimensions at higher frequencies give higher Q)
exp: At higher microwave frequencies, cavity resonators can be made smaller while achieving higher Q factors than lumped-element LC circuits.

q: What law provides regulation of the ownership and operation of radio and television stations and for other purposes?
What is the IBM Token Ring network split pair speed?
exp: IBM Token Ring (IEEE 802.5) operates at 4 Mbps or 16 Mbps. It uses token passing to avoid collisions. Maximum nodes: 260. It's largely been replaced by Ethernet.

q: The system in Fig. 4-9 remains at rest when FW  220 N. What are the magnitude and direction of the friction force on the 200-N block?
exp: Schaum's College Physics - Equilibrium

q: What do you call the resistance of the diode when operating at a steady state voltage?
What is the GPS satellite orbit altitude?
exp: GPS satellites orbit at 20,200 km (Medium Earth Orbit). This height provides global coverage while keeping the orbit period at 12 hours.

q: What is RS-422 and its data rate?
a: Balanced differential interface standard, up to 10 Mbps at 1200 meters
exp: RS-422 uses differential signaling for noise immunity and can achieve 10 Mbps over distances up to 1200 meters.

q: What is the frequency difference between the color subcarrier and the sound carrier in NTSC TV?
exp: The NTSC audio carrier is at 4.5 MHz above the video carrier; the color subcarrier is at 3.58 MHz above the video carrier, a difference of 0.92 MHz.

q: What is slope overload in delta modulation?
a: An error when the analog signal changes too rapidly for the delta modulation system to track
exp: Slope overload occurs when the signal slope exceeds the maximum tracking rate of the delta modulator, causing distortion in fast-changing signals.

q: What is the S-unit in radio signal reporting?
exp: Each S-unit = 6 dB signal strength change. S9 = 50 microvolts at the antenna terminal. S9+10dB means 10 dB above S9. The logarithmic scale matches human auditory perception and the AGC characteristics of radio receivers.

q: What frequency range does the Marconi antenna operate best at?
exp: The Marconi antenna (quarter-wave vertical with ground plane) is most practical at lower frequencies (below 2 MHz) due to its large physical size.

q: What is the gamma of a TV picture tube?
exp: TV picture tubes have a non-linear response described by gamma (γ = 2.2), which must be compensated by gamma correction in the camera.

q: A car must attain a speed of 65 kph for zero side thrust. If coefficient of friction is 0.60, what maximum safe speed at which the car can go without sliding up the curvature of the 100 m radius?

A businessman bought a communication equipment costing P25000 payable in 10 semi-annual payments, each installment payable at the beginning of each period. If rate of interest is 26% compounded semi-annually, what is the amount of each installment?
At what frequency does a magnetron microwave oven operate?
exp: Microwave ovens use 2.45 GHz because water molecules absorb energy efficiently at this frequency. The ISM (Industrial, Scientific, Medical) band at 2.4 GHz is license-free internationally.

q: What weight in pounds can be lifted by a screw that has an efficiency of 80% if it is operated by a 50 lb force at the end of a 30 inched lever and the pitch of the screw is ½ inch?

What is the frequency separation between forward and reverse channels in cellular?
exp: AMPS uses 824–849 MHz (reverse/mobile-to-base) and 869–894 MHz (forward/base-to-mobile), with 45 MHz duplex spacing between them.

q: A simply supported beam, 10 m long carries a uniform distributed load of 20 kN/m. What is the value of the maximum moment of the beam due to the load?
What is the shifting of antenna pattern so that the major lobe is at an angle below horizontal?
exp: Antenna downtilt (electrical or mechanical) aims the main beam slightly downward, reducing range while improving coverage within the cell. This reduces co-channel interference in cellular networks.

q: What satellite subsystem senses the angle of solar radiation to compute satellite orientation?
exp: Sun sensors are attitude determination devices. By measuring the angle of sunlight incidence, the satellite's computer can calculate its orientation relative to the sun.

q: The first law of thermodynamics is based on which of the following principles?
What body coordinates government and military communications in the USA?
exp: The NTIA manages the federal government's use of the radio frequency spectrum and advises the President on telecommunications policy.

q: What multiplexing technique does PCM use?
exp: PCM digitizes voice signals and multiplexes them using TDM, where each channel gets a time slot in the digital frame.

q: What do you call a negatively charged ion?
The velocity of sound depends on which factors?
exp: Sound speed increases with temperature (≈0.6 m/s per °C in air) and varies by medium (faster in denser solids/liquids). Pressure alone has minimal effect in gases.

q: What is the data rate of TDMA in D-AMPS?
exp: D-AMPS (IS-136) uses TDMA to divide each 30 kHz channel into three 8 kbps time slots, tripling the capacity of AMPS.

q: What is the Faraday screen used for?
a: Minimize losses / prevent transmitter harmonic radiation
exp: A Faraday screen (cage) surrounds a transmitter to prevent unwanted RF radiation (harmonics). It's also used in transformers between primary and secondary windings to reduce electrostatic coupling while allowing magnetic coupling.

q: Which of the following is NOT a porous absorber?
exp: Porous absorbers include fiberglass and foam. Membrane absorbers work by vibration of thin panels, not pore-based sound absorption.

q: What ITU standard covers the V.34bis facsimile?
exp: V.34bis extends the V.34 modem standard to 33.6 kbps, significantly improving fax transmission speed over standard telephone lines.

q: What is vertical antenna stacking?
a: Reduces vertical beamwidth, increases horizontal gain
exp: Stacking antennas collinearly compresses the vertical radiation pattern, concentrating energy toward the horizon. Each doubling of elements adds approximately 3 dBd gain. FM broadcast stations use 4-8 element vertical stacks for maximum coverage.

q: What navigation system provides 88-98% global coverage?
exp: Omega was a VLF (10-14 kHz) hyperbolic radio navigation system with 8 stations worldwide. Decommissioned in 1997 and replaced by GPS. It provided positional accuracy of 1-2 nautical miles globally.

q: What is conversational service in B-ISDN?
a: Real-time bidirectional communication service (e.g., video conferencing)
exp: Conversational service in B-ISDN supports real-time two-way exchanges like video telephony, requiring low delay and synchronization.

q: The Q-point of a class D amplifier can be set or positioned at what region in the load line?
What frequency range is used for aircraft long-range HF communications?
exp: HF radio (2–30 MHz) is used for long-distance aircraft communications, especially over oceans where VHF line-of-sight is insufficient.

q: What test is used to test AM transmitters using SSB method?
exp: The two-tone test applies two equal-amplitude audio tones (e.g., 700 Hz and 1900 Hz) to a transmitter. The resulting intermodulation products reveal linearity. For SSB, the output should be two clean carriers with no IMD products.

q: What is the data rate of an ISDN B channel?
exp: Each ISDN B (Bearer) channel carries 64 kbps, suitable for one voice call or data transmission using PCM.

q: What is the in-phase (I) signal phase angle in NTSC color?
exp: The NTSC I signal is transmitted at 57° phase from the color burst reference, and the Q signal at 147°. This arrangement optimizes for the eye's varying color resolution.

q: a constant velocity. What is thus constant velocity called?
Which is not a bit-oriented protocol?
exp: BISYNC (Binary Synchronous Communications) is a character-oriented (byte-oriented) protocol developed by IBM. HDLC, SDLC, and LLC are bit-oriented protocols using flag fields.

q: What is the LED usually used as a signal source for plastic fiber?
exp: Red LEDs (~650 nm) are used with plastic optical fiber because POF has lowest attenuation in the red wavelength range, and red LEDs are inexpensive and efficient.

q: An electron strikes the screen of the cathode ray tube with a velocity of 10 to the 9th power cm/s. Compute its kinetic energy in erg. The mass of an electron is 9 x 10^-31 kg?
What is equal power per octave noise called?
exp: Pink noise (also called flicker noise) has equal power per octave — each doubling of frequency contains equal energy. White noise has equal power per Hz.

q: In a magnet, what do you call the point in which the magnetic lines of force is maximum?
What is the characteristic impedance of standard TV coaxial cable?
exp: TV distribution systems use 75-ohm coaxial cable (e.g., RG-6) for minimum signal loss. Lab/transmitter equipment uses 50-ohm coax.

q: An automobile moving at 30 m/s is approaching a building whistle with a frequency of 500 Hz. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s what is the apparent frequency of the whistle heard by the driver?
What is the threshold effect in FM reception?
a: The noise-reduction improvement that occurs when the FM signal exceeds the threshold level (~10 dB above noise)
exp: Above the FM threshold, the discriminator output has much less noise than the input SNR would suggest — FM provides a noise advantage when the signal is sufficiently strong.

q: What radio system is used to provide high-speed data packet access for GSM?
exp: General Packet Radio Service (GPRS) is a packet-switched overlay on GSM, providing data rates up to ~172 kbps. It enables always-on internet access without a dedicated circuit.

q: What best describes the transistor current that flows between the collector and emitter terminals when the base is open?

A man driving his car at a constant rate of 40 mph suddenly sees a sheep crossing the road 60 feet ahead. Compute the constant deceleration (in feet/second2) required to avoid hitting the sheep? Assume a reaction time of 0.5 second before the man applies the brake.

What is the frequency of an alternating current, if it reaches 90° within 4.167 ms?
What is the total charge at the nucleus of silicon atom?

What semiconductor diode that have a fine wire (called a cat-whisker) whose point is in permanent contact with the surface of a wafer of semiconductor material such as silicon, germanium or gallium arsenide?
What is CDMA2000 1xRTT data rate?
exp: CDMA2000 1xRTT (1x Radio Transmission Technology) provides 153 kbps peak data rate, meeting the 3G threshold. EV-DO Rev 0 reached 2.4 Mbps and EV-DO Rev A reached 3.1 Mbps download. Used by Verizon and Sprint before 4G LTE.

q: A 900-kg car whose motor delivers a maximum power of 40.0 hp to its wheels can maintain a steady speed of 130 km/h on a horizontal roadway. How large is the friction force that impedes its motion at this speed?
exp: Schaum's College Physics - Projectile Motion

q: In general, which of the transistors is particularly more useful in integrated-circuit (IC) chips?
What law states that it is impossible to operate an engine operating in a cycle that will have no other effect than to extract heat from a reservoir and turn it into an equivalent amount of work?
What is the bulk modulus of steel if the sound waves traveled at approximately 5900 m/s? Note: the density of steel is 7900 kg/m^3
What is radiation exposure from a TV receiver at 5 cm?
exp: FCC requires TV receivers to not exceed 0.5 mR/hour at 5 cm from any surface, and 0.1 mR/hour at 5 cm from TV CRT (X-ray from high-voltage electron beam).

q: What devices are inserted into a telephone channel if total via net loss exceeds about 2.5 dB?
exp: Echo suppressors insert one-way loss in the return path to reduce echo on long-distance calls. They create a half-duplex condition. Echo cancellers (active DSP) replaced them on modern networks.

q: What percentage of Earth's surface can a single GEO satellite cover at 0° elevation?
exp: A geostationary satellite at 0° minimum elevation can see roughly 42.4% of Earth's surface. Three such satellites with overlapping coverage can serve almost the entire globe.

q: What is Benjamin Franklin's contribution to electrical science?
a: Established that lightning is electrical and identified two types of electric charge (positive and negative)
exp: Franklin's kite experiment proved lightning is electricity, and he coined the terms positive and negative charge, as well as inventing the lightning rod.

q: What happens in the resistance of copper wire when its temperature is raised?
What type of transmission line uses a ground return?
exp: Unbalanced lines like coax use one conductor as signal and the other (outer shield/ground) as return path.

q: What device amplifies by interaction between an electron beam and an RF field along a linear path?
exp: TWTs use a helical slow-wave structure to match the electron beam velocity with the RF wave, enabling continuous amplification over a wide bandwidth. Used in satellite transponders and radar amplifiers.

q: What is the formula for REM?
exp: REM (Roentgen Equivalent Man) = RBE (Relative Biological Effectiveness) × RAD (Radiation Absorbed Dose). Alpha particles: RBE=10; Beta/gamma: RBE=1. REM accounts for biological impact.

q: What is the purpose of cooling a parametric amplifier?
a: To improve noise performance (reduce thermal noise)
exp: Parametric amplifiers achieve extremely low noise figures when cooled to near absolute zero, making them ideal for satellite receivers and radio telescopes.

q: What color in visible light has the longest wavelength after red?
exp: The visible spectrum in order of decreasing wavelength: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet (ROY G BIV). Orange follows red as second longest.

q: The atomic weight of a silicon atom is approximately 28 amu. How many electrons, protons and neutrons does the atom consist?
If in Fig. 4-9 the friction between the block and the incline is negligible, how much must the object on the right weigh if the 200-N block is to remain at rest?
exp: Schaum's College Physics - Equilibrium

q: What law that describes the force of attraction or repulsion between two magnetic poles is directly proportional to their strengths?
In a TV system, what signal has information for 1.3 MHz bandwidth?

What is a vocoder?

What is the position accuracy of LORAN C/D?
exp: LORAN C/D achieves position accuracy of approximately 460 meters (0.25 nautical miles), sufficient for maritime and aviation en-route navigation.

q: What is Michael Faraday known for?
a: Discovering electromagnetic induction and the unit of capacitance (Farad) is named after him
exp: Faraday showed that a changing magnetic field induces an electric current, the principle behind generators and transformers. He also invented the Faraday cage.

q: What is the technique used to spread a signal by linearly shifting the carrier frequency?
exp: Chirp (linear frequency modulation) sweeps the carrier frequency linearly across a bandwidth. Used in radar for pulse compression — sending a long chirped pulse and compressing it on receive for high range resolution.

exp: Schaum's College Physics - Newton's Laws

q: When was the first analog cellular phone call made commercially?
exp: The first commercial analog cellular service (AMPS) launched on October 13, 1983 in Chicago by Ameritech, using 800 MHz frequencies.

q: What did Alessandro Volta invent?
a: The voltaic pile (1796) — the first electric battery
exp: Volta's voltaic pile, made of alternating zinc and copper discs separated by brine-soaked cloth, was the first device to produce a continuous electric current.

q: In TV, special effects and production switching are done by?
exp: A Special Effects Generator (SEG) is video production equipment for mixing, switching, and applying effects between multiple video sources.

q: Which color contributes the most luminance in a video signal?
exp: Yellow has the highest luminance because the human eye is most sensitive to green and red; yellow is the additive mix of these two primaries.

q: What is the modulation used in Enhanced Data Rate for GSM Evolution (EDGE)?
exp: EDGE uses 8-PSK modulation (3 bits per symbol), tripling the bit rate compared to GMSK used in standard GPRS. EDGE provides data rates up to 384 kbps.

q: What routing technique requires each node to retransmit packets onto every outgoing line?
exp: Flooding ensures packets reach their destination by sending them on all routes. It's reliable but inefficient. Used in military and some mesh networks where reliability trumps efficiency.

q: A force of 20 N is acting on a 10 Wb magnetic pole, calculate the intensity of the magnetic field?
What is the Gunn effect?
a: Oscillations produced in GaAs (gallium arsenide) at microwave frequencies due to transferred electron effect
exp: Gunn diodes exploit the negative resistance in GaAs when an electric field causes electrons to transfer to higher-energy, lower-mobility states, producing microwave oscillations.

q: What is the output terminal match loss in CATV systems?
exp: CATV distribution equipment maintains output terminal-to-terminal isolation of typically 16 dB to prevent reflections from one outlet affecting others.

q: Why must a parametric amplifier be cooled?
exp: The noise temperature of a parametric amplifier decreases dramatically when cooled; at liquid helium temperatures (~4K), noise temperatures below 10K are achievable for satellite receivers.

q: What is defined as the direct conversion of a substance from the solid to the vapor state or vice versa without passing the liquid state?
What is the lowest layer of the ionosphere?
exp: The ionosphere has D, E, F1, and F2 layers. F1 is the lower portion of the F layer and is most prominent during the day.

q: How is fiber grating produced?
a: By illuminating the fiber with ultraviolet light
exp: Fiber Bragg Gratings (FBG) are created by exposing photosensitive fiber to a UV interference pattern. This creates periodic refractive index variations that act as wavelength-selective reflectors.

q: When was the Strowger automatic telephone exchange switch invented?
exp: Almon Strowger invented the step-by-step (Strowger) switch in 1889 and it became commercially available around 1892-1897, enabling automatic telephone dialing.

q: What does TACAN provide?
a: Bearing and distance (slant range) information for aircraft navigation
exp: TACAN (Tactical Air Navigation) provides both azimuth (bearing) and DME (distance) for military aircraft navigation.

q: What is the Adaptive Multi-Rate (AMR) codec?
a: Variable rate speech codec for 3G systems from 4.75 to 12.2 kbps
exp: AMR adjusts its coding rate based on channel quality: high rate for good signal gives better voice quality, low rate for poor signal provides more error correction bits. Standard voice codec for UMTS (3G) and enhanced GSM networks.

What is the minimum illumination level recommended for reading?
exp: Adequate reading illumination is typically 500-1000 lux in practice, but 8000 lux is cited as the minimum for comfortable reading in some standards.

q: What is return loss when termination impedance equals characteristic impedance?
exp: When load impedance perfectly matches characteristic impedance, all power is absorbed and none is reflected, giving infinite return loss.

q: Why is FM more efficient than AM?
a: Because FM uses class C amplifiers
exp: FM transmitters use highly efficient Class C amplifiers (70-85% efficiency) because FM has constant amplitude. AM requires linear Class A/B amplifiers (~25-50% efficiency) to preserve amplitude variations.

q: What is the color burst frequency in NTSC?
exp: The NTSC color subcarrier is precisely 3.579545 MHz, chosen to interleave with the luminance spectrum and minimize visible dot pattern interference.

exp: OSI Layer 1 (Physical) deals with voltages, current levels, bit timing, and physical connectors. It transmits raw bits over the medium — nothing about meaning or structure.

q: What is the orbital period of each GPS constellation satellite?
exp: GPS satellites orbit at 20,200 km altitude with a 12-hour period. Six orbital planes are spaced 60° apart, each inclined 55° relative to the equator.

exp: At night, the F2 layer persists (unlike E and F1 layers which disappear). A single F2 hop can cover up to 4130 km, enabling long-distance HF communication at night.

a: The frequency at which the VCO oscillates when its control voltage is zero

q: What is Photometry?
a: Science of measuring light visible to the human eye

a: Area between outer ground wave range and inner edge of ionospheric return

q: What are pulses that retain their shapes as they pass through optical fibers?
exp: Solitons are optical pulses that maintain their shape by balancing fiber dispersion with nonlinear effects (self-phase modulation). They enable ultra-long-distance transmission without distortion.

exp: By Nyquist's theorem, binary transmission maximum rate = 2 × bandwidth = 2 × 36 MHz = 72 Mbps. Higher-order modulation achieves more, but this is the binary limit.
